why: The agent lane's preview verdict, written once and read by two implementations: the Rust law `app::agent_lane_preview_tests` (`🧪️tests/🤖️agent-lane-preview/🦀️.rs`) drives a scripted job through the real driver `drive_agent_lane_preview` — the SAME caller-driven worker session every app-owned job the MCP gateway's `action_prepare` reaches runs in (the SDK's retained command, a plugin's own tool-command job such as puzzle's or writer's) — and the AJV twin (`🧪️tests/🤖️agent-lane-preview/🟦️.ts`, run by the SDK's `test` script) derives the verdict from the same script with one JSON Schema per outcome kind. A script lists what each step of the job reports (`progress`, `checkpoint`, `yield`, `complete`, `cancelled`, or a `fault` with the job's own detail bytes); the job repeats its last entry forever. The rules: the verdict is the first terminal entry — `complete` at position n answers `steps: n` (every outcome the job reported up to and including its completion); `cancelled` or a lease cancelled before the run (`cancelled: true`) answers `interactive-job.cancelled`; a `fault` answers the typed record its detail carries (`semio.typed-operation-fault.v1`, `🧬️schema/🧯️typed-operation-fault/🔣️.json` — a script writes it as an object): the record's own code, origin and message; any other detail — framed text or prose included, a record is never split out of text — answers `interactive-job.app-owned-output` under origin `framework` with the detail as its message; a script without a terminal entry is refused `interactive-job.preview-budget` whether the wall budget or the turn budget ends it. `clockMicrosPerRead` is the harness clock only (0 freezes it, so the turn budget ends the run).

cases.name: a job that completes after its own progress answers every outcome up to its completion
a job that completes on its first step answers one step
a job fault that carries no typed record keeps its own detail under the app-owned output code
